Simple implementation of the well-known series of wave functions known as spherical harmonics, which are defined in spherical coordinates and thus define 3D volumes.

http://paulbourke.net/geometry/sphericalh/

(Part of my series of reference implementations of classic algorithms...)

visuals.title: Kinect 3D scanner
visuals.description:
Simple 3D scanner using the Kinect.

Doesn't work in the browser. You need a Kinect to run it and the controlP5 (version controlP5_1.5.1), hemesh and simple-openni libraries installed. 
 
Select the scanner area with the controls and press the "take scan" button to capture the 3D points inside the box. A mesh is created with the Hemesh library and saved in the sketch directory. The colors of the mesh faces are saved in a different file. Press the "take scan" button again to take more scans. 
 
Use http://www.openprocessing.org/sketch/62533 to read and represent the mesh.

visuals.title: fibonacci_sphere
visuals.description:
A fast method of producing an arbitrary number of equally distributed points around a sphere.  This is accomplished by drawing a fibonacci spiral (similar to sunflower seed pattern) that maintains constant surface area.

n = number of points
phi = (sqrt(5)+1)/2 - 1
ga = PHI * TWO_PI

for each point i (1..n)
    longitude = ga*i
    latitude = asin(-1 + 2*i/n)

As written, the sketch constantly adds new points to the sphere.  Click to toggle this feature, so you can examine the point distribution.

It was the basis for the RD/TD system described by John Whitney in his 1980 book Digital Harmony.

visuals.title: Noise flow Painter
visuals.description:
*It may need a moment to load*

Paints an image with strokes that are rotated by a flow field driven from noise.

If you want to try it on your own image you need to drag and drop an image in the sketch's files tab. Then add your image's file name to the variable imgNames (it's near the top). It doesn't capture details very well so close ups work best.

Controls:
  - Click to change to the next image.
  - Press any key to save the canvas to a jpg.
visuals.instructions: Click for the next image, press a key to save a jpg.

visuals.title: Volcanic cascades
visuals.description:
A combination of my two older sketches:
Waterfall cascades: https://www.openprocessing.org/sketch/396286
Frozen brush: https://www.openprocessing.org/sketch/413567

Uses the physics from the waterfall sketch, and renders it with delaunay triangulation.
I did NOT develop delaunay.js, and not sure who the author really is to give proper credit.

Controls:
  - Move the mouse around to interact with the particles.
  - Use the on-screen controls to effect the sim.
visuals.instructions: Check the description.

visuals.title: Noise flow Painter
visuals.description:
*It may need a moment to load*

Paints an image with strokes that are rotated by a flow field driven from noise.

If you want to try it on your own image you need to drag and drop an image in the sketch's files tab. Then add your image's file name to the variable imgNames (it's near the top). It doesn't capture details very well so close ups work best.

Controls:
  - Click to change to the next image.
  - Press any key to save the canvas to a jpg.
visuals.instructions: Click for the next image, press a key to save a jpg.

visuals.title: Volcanic cascades
visuals.description:
A combination of my two older sketches:
Waterfall cascades: https://www.openprocessing.org/sketch/396286
Frozen brush: https://www.openprocessing.org/sketch/413567

Uses the physics from the waterfall sketch, and renders it with delaunay triangulation.
I did NOT develop delaunay.js, and not sure who the author really is to give proper credit.

Controls:
  - Move the mouse around to interact with the particles.
  - Use the on-screen controls to effect the sim.
visuals.instructions: Check the description.

FinalProject_Craige
visuals.description: Moon phases can be difficult to understand. But, it may help to see a representation of some! Moon phases are the different phases of the moon that we humans see from the perspective of earth. Space is so dark, so if it weren't for the sun, we wouldn't be able to see the moon, or space at all. The part of the moon that we actually see is the side of the moon that is shone on by the sun's light. The reason that we see it differently every day is that as the moon orbits the earth and rotates at that same rate, we see it at different angles. It also depends on where you are on earth.
visuals.instructions: Scroll over the screen to see some of the moon phases appear, and click to see what moon phases are.

visuals.description: This symbol is called the ichthys from the Greek ikhthys. It was used by early Christians and resembles a fish mostly alluding to passage in the Bible in which Jesus called out to two fishermen Simon and his brother Andrew who immediately left their nets to follow him. Jesus said to them "Follow Me, and I will make you fishers of men." The youth group at my church also uses this symbol.

visuals.title: Delaunay Subdivision
visuals.description:
(unoptimized) Delaunay triangulation with various display modes.
The graphic starts with two triangles. Each frame new triangles are added. visuals.title: Maze Generator: Randomized Kruskal's Algorithm迷宫
visuals.description:
Another maze generation program. This is one is a lot less fun than the last one but the code is a lot tidier and there is now a working solver. 

For more resources on Kruskal's algorithm, see:
* http://weblog.jamisbuck.org/2011/1/3/maze-generation-kruskal-s-algorithm
* https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maze_generation_algorithm#Randomized_Kruskal's_algorithm
Basically, it puts the cells into sets, which are all merged (by removing a wall between them) until all the cells are connected. The colors you see are the sets.

Kruskal's algorithm generates perfect mazes with a uniform spanning tree.

a - toggle AutoPaint (on/off)
1,2,3,4 - change color-source image
          stored as square "001.jpg" etc, in the data folder
g - paint a grid of text covering entire screen (may take a while in .js)
m/M - change paint Mode (the default mode takes color from images)
s - save
x - change black/white mode
c - clear screen

visuals.description:
Our version of an Italian Word Search using the most common Italian words used in restaurants. Once the user finds a word they can draw a straight line through the letters. Identical to the way a hard copy word search works, they can strike out the found word from the list to the right. There is also a timer function that shows the time passed since the game has started. When the timer gets to 12.59.59 a funny phrase will be printed on the screen.
Every time the game starts a different grid will be printed on the screen.
Click&hold; with left mouse button to draw a line.

visuals.title: Oil-water phase separation
visuals.description:
A 2D model of how oil and water molecules repel each other with different strengths, making them self-assemble into groups. Based on the PhD thesis of Naoaki Ono.

The mouse controls a water molecule so you can push the oil blobs around.

If you want to play it as a game, try this:

Task 1: push all the blobs together into one big blob.

Task 2: split the big blob into little blobs. You get more points for the more separate blobs you make.

(Note: there aren't any points, you will have to make up your own scoring system.)
visuals.instructions: Move the mouse to push the oil blobs around

visuals.title: quasicrystals
visuals.description:
Points are added by the user drawing on the screen, in principle forming a line.

But these points don't remain still, each point will slowly move away from its nearest neighbour.

A line from each point to its nearest neighbour is drawn, the color depending on the length.

The user can navigate through the view by pressing '+' and '-' (zoom) and the arrow keys (pan). The space bar sets the view still again.

visuals.title: 大量のキューブ
visuals.description:
インタラクションのある作品を作るということで、今回僕はスライドバーでX.Y.Zの回転を自由に変更することができる作品を作りました。スライドバーは今回初めて使ったのですが1時間で理解でき、綺麗に組み込むことができてよかったです。
苦労した点：この作品を作るにあたってsin.cosを初めて使ったので、使い方を理解するのに苦労しました。
工夫した点：キューブに色をつけました。というのも、色の付け方がわからなくて、普段使うfill();だと色がつかず最終的にambientMaterialを使って色をつけられました。

作った作品をセーブしていたら、Richard Bourneさんが僕の作品に写真機能を加えたものを作っていていました。https://openprocessing.org/sketch/1217598

参考：https://p5js.org/examples/3d-sine-cosine-in-3d.html

visuals.title: Recursive Tree
visuals.description:
Since everybody got one: Here is my version of a recursive Tree. The text you see at the bottom of the sketch is the seed value for the random generator. Change the seed and see what happens.

Controls:
- TYPE SOMETHING = create seed
- MOUSECLICK = create random seed and generate tree
- BACKSPACE/DEL = delete last letter
- RETURN/ENTER/CTRL = confirm your seed and generate tree
- ALT = save image

visuals.title: Maze Generator: Randomized Kruskal's Algorithm
visuals.description:
Another maze generation program. This is one is a lot less fun than the last one but the code is a lot tidier and there is now a working solver. 

For more resources on Kruskal's algorithm, see:
* http://weblog.jamisbuck.org/2011/1/3/maze-generation-kruskal-s-algorithm
* https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maze_generation_algorithm#Randomized_Kruskal's_algorithm
Basically, it puts the cells into sets, which are all merged (by removing a wall between them) until all the cells are connected. The colors you see are the sets.

Kruskal's algorithm generates perfect mazes with a uniform spanning tree.
visuals.instructions: Use the controls on the right. See description for more info.

visuals.title: expressivedance001
visuals.description: Controls: Mouse pressed stops the lines from spiraling inward, and stops showing their paths. Mouse not pressed sends the lines spiraling inward. Also try holding down the mouse and moving it around the screen a bit, and then releasing the mouse and hold it perfectly still, watching what happens. The code is relatively easy to figure out, it's a particle system. Enjoy.

This is my evolution simulator! I uploaded some videos of this simulator to my YouTube channel carykh: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GOFws_hhZs8

It runs about 3x faster in the Java version.

Also: the JS version might have trouble drawing rectangles.  If that happens, disable hardware acceleration in your browser.
For the java version: you need to create the font that it uses.  Just go to Tools...   create font... Helvetica-Bold, and set the font size to 96.  The file name should already be "Helvetica-Bold-96.vlw".
